title: Cards the daemon no longer holds stay on screen; reconcile only adds
body:
## Summary
`reconcile()` merges `GET /decisions` into the cards as a union, so a card the daemon expired or that was answered on another surface (voice, the other window) stays on screen and in the pill's "N waiting" until the person presses it.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:1690` (`reconcile`) calls `mergeCards` (`run.ts:938`), which keeps every current card and only adds pending rows. `startRun` (`run.ts:1790`) re-reads every 30 s while any card is on screen, but nothing it reads can take a card away. Only `decision.resolved` on the stream of a turn in flight, or a refused answer with `unknown_ref` (`run.ts:1439`), removes one. Fixed: a card that was on screen when the read started and is absent from a COMPLETE pending page is dropped (with a line saying it is no longer waiting). The catch: `GET /decisions` is paginated (`src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1048`, `limit` bounded, `total` up to PENDING_CEILING), so absence from a page with `showing < total` proves nothing, and a card arriving on the stream after the request left must survive the response. Technique: hitl-approval/review-queues ("badge count disagrees with what the queue shows"), client-state/invalidation-strategy.

## Flow
- a card is filed; the person answers it by voice (stores/voice.ts removes it there) or it expires in the daemon
- the panel's 30 s reconcile reads GET /decisions without it
- mergeCards keeps it; the pill says 1 waiting; pressing it is refused unknown_ref and only then drops it
- fix order: capture ids before the read; drop only ids present before, absent from the page, page complete (showing == total), and not answering

## Expected impact
6

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the card list and the pill count match what the daemon holds
Before: mergeCards([card], [], () => false) returns [card]: a card absent from the pending page is never dropped (read at run.ts:938-966)
After: predicted: dropped when the page is complete and the card predates the read; kept when showing < total or the card arrived mid-read
Method: simulation - three cases walked (voice answer, expiry, a stream card racing the read); the instrument is a run.test.ts case set over mergeCards with a page whose showing < total, not built because the union is the documented contract and the paging rule needs the daemon's limit semantics confirmed
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:938-966 mergeCards keeps `current` whole: `const kept = current.map(...)`; only `added` grows it.
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:1690-1708 reconcile: `cards: mergeCards(s.cards, page.pending ?? [], skip)`.
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1048-1051 `limit = bounded(request.query.get("limit"))` ... `rows[:limit]`, `announced(rows, page.total, "pending")`.
instrument: run.test.ts cases: a complete pending page without a pre-existing card drops it; a page with showing < total keeps it; a card streamed while GET /decisions is in flight survives the response

title: A re-ask of a page already read blanks its tool list until the page answers
body:
## Summary
`useTools.refresh` writes an empty `asking` placeholder over a tab's known tools on every re-ask, so a turn snapshotted during a toolchange re-read publishes a manifest with no tools for that page.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/tools.ts:78` sets `byTab[tabId] = blank(tabId, url)` before every `bridgeList`, including a `bridge:toolchange` re-read of the SAME document. `snapshotOf` (`apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:678`) builds the manifest from `byTab[tab].tools`; during the round trip that is `[]`, and `POST /manifest` replaces the origin's catalog entries (`merge_manifest`), so the turn sees no page tools. The placeholder exists so a NEW tab reads as asking, not empty; a re-read of a known document could keep the last list with `asking: true`. Technique: client-state/status-fsms (a refresh is not a first load).

## Flow
- a page registers a tool after load and fires bridge:toolchange
- refresh(tab) blanks byTab[tab].tools while bridge_list is in flight
- the person sends a message in that window: snapshotOf -> manifest with tools []
- fix: on a re-ask of the same url keep tools/appId/transport and set asking:true

## Expected impact
5

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a turn never publishes an empty manifest for a page whose tools are known
Before: tools.ts:78 replaces the entry with blank(...) on every refresh; a snapshot between that write and the answer has tools [] (read)
After: predicted: the snapshot carries the last known list
Method: simulation - three cases (toolchange during idle, during send, a navigation which must still blank); the instrument is a run.test.ts + tools.test.ts pair, not built because the robustness-1 snapshot tests pin the blank-entry behaviour and need a worker to re-read them
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/stores/tools.ts:76-78 `set({ byTab: { ...get().byTab, [tabId]: blank(tabId, url) } });` (tools: [], asking: true).
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:690-701 snapshotOf: `tools: found?.tools ?? []` into manifestBodyOf.
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.test.ts:1380 'a refresh that blanks the entry after the manifest ...' pins the related robustness case.
instrument: tools.test.ts: a toolchange re-ask of the same url keeps the previous tools with asking:true; run.test.ts: snapshotOf taken mid re-ask names the known tools

title: startTabs' first list can land after a newer tabs:changed and overwrite it
body:
## Summary
`startTabs` subscribes to `tabs:changed`, then awaits `tabsList()` and writes its answer unconditionally, so a change event delivered before the command's answer is overwritten by the older list.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/tabs.ts:447-449`: the listener writes every event's list; then `const tabs = await tabsList(); useTabs.setState(...)`. Tauri delivers events and command answers on separate paths with no ordering between them, so a tab opened by ATHENA_START_URL (the case the comment names) can arrive as an event first and be erased by the command's earlier snapshot until the next change. Fixed: once any event has been applied, the initial list is dropped (a latest-wins flag). Technique: client-state/async-race-guards.

## Flow
- startTabs subscribes, asks tabs_list
- Rust answers tabs_list with [A], then emits tabs:changed [A,B]; the event is handled first
- the command's [A] resolves and replaces [A,B]; tools/run read a tab list missing B

## Expected impact
3

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the first tab list never replaces a newer one
Before: tabs.ts:448-449 writes the tabsList answer with no check (read)
After: predicted: dropped when an event was applied after the subscription
Method: simulation - delivery order between a Tauri command answer and an event is not reproducible in vitest without asserting the shell's ordering; the instrument is a tabs.test.ts with the ipc mock firing the event before resolving tabs_list
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/stores/tabs.ts:447 `await onTabsChanged((tabs) => useTabs.setState(...))`
apps/desktop/src/stores/tabs.ts:448-449 `const tabs = await tabsList(); useTabs.setState((s) => ({ tabs, loaded: true, ... }))`
instrument: new tabs.test.ts: ipc mock fires tabs:changed [A,B] while tabs_list is pending, then resolves [A]; expect [A,B]

title: A settings write that fails leaves the choice painted and held but not stored
body:
## Summary
Every settings setter moves the state (and paints) before `settingWrite`, and nothing restores it when the write rejects, so the window shows a theme, engine or project that the store never took.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/settings.ts:105-148`: `setEngine`, `setTheme`, `setTypeScale`, `setMotion`, `setActiveProject`, `setBrainPath`, `setOnboarded` all `set(...)` first and `await settingWrite(...)` after, with no catch. The paint-first order is deliberate (the comment at 110-112), but a failed write leaves state and store disagreeing until the next store:changed, and `setOnboarded`'s early-return guard then refuses to write the same value again. Fixed: on rejection, re-read the rows (`readRows`, which now never rejects) so the window shows what is stored, and rethrow for the caller's report. Technique: settings/save-experience ("toggle stays flipped after a failed write"), client-state/optimistic-write-path.

## Flow
- the person picks Light; applyTheme paints it; settingWrite rejects (store locked)
- the caller reports the error, but the theme stays Light and useSettings.theme says light
- next launch reads the stored dark: the choice silently reverts
- fix: catch -> await readRows() -> rethrow

## Expected impact
4

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - after a failed write the state equals the stored row
Before: settings.ts:105-148 has no rollback path (read); a failing store_set leaves useSettings.theme on the unsaved value
After: predicted: theme back to the stored value, error still surfaced to the caller
Method: simulation - three setters walked; the instrument is a settings.test.ts case with store_set failing, not built this round to keep within the budget after nine builds
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/stores/settings.ts:113-118 setTheme: applyTheme -> set -> useShell.setState -> await settingWrite (no catch)
apps/desktop/src/stores/settings.ts:144-148 setOnboarded: `if (get().onboarded === onboarded) return;` before the write
instrument: settings.test.ts: harness.failing for store_set on settings/theme; setTheme('light') rejects and useSettings.theme / data-theme return to the stored value
